: **Measurements that would move the verdict toward `COND`**: Each row names the premise a measurement settles on the warehouse mobile manipulator and the restriction a supporting result would lift; the inference trace bears on service availability only. {#tbl-16-cond-measurements tbl-colwidths="[20,30,8,42]"}

Inference latency contributes to the useful-service case. Its overruns need not defeat protection when the independent permission path and powered fallback survive the stated fault, but they can prevent timely delivery. Shared-resource interference that delays the enforcer or its observations is a separate C2/C5 failure. Local operation can omit unused remote-channel trials; it still needs the placement ledger, common-cause coverage, and passing authority trials for every local transition exercised.

### Worked restricted service with stipulated evidence {#sec-release-stipulated-service}

The following branch is **STIPULATED**, not a report of tests performed on the textbook machine. Its purpose is to complete the adjudication: assume a reviewed packet supplies the evidence specified below, while retaining the existing selected limits. The actual evidence in this book still supports `REFUSE`.

The proposed service is *restricted inspected-route mug delivery*: collect the declared mug from the controlled, singulated feed, carry it along the assessed aisle route at no more than `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_restricted_str`, open the nominal cage latch at the guarded approach with the base stopped, and hand the mug to a consenting coworker under `accept_item` at `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_handover_str`. Authority remains local. The feed regime excludes indistinguishable substitutions; singulation alone does not prove identity. The crossing regime excludes continued human approach into the stopping corridor, and assessed access controls maintain that condition throughout transit.

For C1, stipulate configuration-matched loaded stopping, tracking, localization, latch-stop, and assessed handover-contact records that support the restricted bounds in @tbl-16-cond-measurements. For C2 and C5, stipulate independent fault traces and timing analysis under the declared worst load, including common causes, that support the permission deadline and response onset. Those records distinguish powered deceleration from brake application at rest and establish the drive-energy and sensing premises for the credited faults. For C4, stipulate end-to-end timestamp evidence with clock uncertainty and a qualified bound on dispatch-to-admission delay. Charge that delay to the stopping budget and require a positive declared reserve after charging it; the displayed partial ceiling alone cannot authorize the selected speed. Evidence continues aging through execution, and the lease starts only at successful admission. The capability packet also qualifies successful-admission spacing against the renewal contract, rather than equating inference cadence with accepted renewal. For C6, stipulate `PASS` records for all authority transitions used by this local service; the remote channel remains disabled.

C3 needs more than a dry-floor photograph or a lower speed. Stipulate a qualified floor assessment establishing at least `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_inspected_str` over the named route, plus validated cleaning, contamination isolation, and controlled access that preserve this state for the signed inspection interval. Loaded stopping trials cover that friction floor. Stipulate that the complete restricted stopping budget, including the qualified admission-delay bound and positive required reserve, fits the surveyed clearance. The selected `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_restricted_str` is below the displayed `{python} ReleaseWorkedVerdict.v_inspected_ceiling_str` partial ceiling, but that comparison is only a preliminary screen. A spill report, expired inspection, or loss of access control withdraws the route permit before entry. If unnoticed oil can enter during the authorized interval, this stipulation fails and the worked verdict returns to `REFUSE`; slowing alone does not exclude oil.

The capability packet is also stipulated. Before trials, the site owner records a minimum completed-delivery success rate, a maximum accepted cycle time, and a maximum rescue-intervention rate in the evaluation record, with the trial population, uncertainty treatment, and acceptance rule. A completed delivery must preserve mug identity and integrity through the final handover. Cycle time includes allowed clamps, waiting at crossings, and ordinary recovery; rescues and aborted deliveries remain in their declared denominators. Stipulate that closed-loop evaluation of this exact restricted configuration satisfies all three criteria. The packet separately reports raw proposer autonomy, whole-machine task success, and protective outcomes. Normal least-change filtering can accompany a successful delivery; it neither conceals a rescued policy failure nor counts as a hazard violation.

We can now derive the hypothetical verdict. The stipulated physical records support C1–C6 only over the restricted mission, and the stipulated evaluation establishes useful service under those same restrictions. The adjudicator therefore selects `COND` for *restricted inspected-route mug delivery*, binds both packets and the maintained conditions to its manifest, and leaves the nominal full-speed and remote modes unsigned. This is a completed conditional argument, not a fabricated release authorization. Removing any relied-on evidence or standing condition changes the result back to `REFUSE`; adding qualified new experience and measurements can support a later, broader case.

::: {#chk-release-refusal-and-path-to-cond .callout-checkpoint title="Refusal and the path to conditional release"}

Before approving a conditional release of the machine, verify your understanding of how a premise, rather than a calculation, decides a claim:

- [ ] **Premise vs. arithmetic**: Can you explain why the calculated latch force at physical braking onset is not in doubt while the door branch of C1 is still refused?
- [ ] **Unsupported approach**: Can you use @eq-release-trip-indentation and @eq-release-coupled-indentation to show why the operating envelope admits only the guarded door approach?
- [ ] **Refusal as a deliverable**: Can you name, for one refused claim, the measurement that would lift it and the restriction that would remain after a supporting result?
:::

## Adversarial Review {#sec-release-adversarial-review}

To see how an adversarial audit operates against a candidate deployment authorization, suppose the measurements of @tbl-16-cond-measurements arrive and support a `COND` case for the mobile manipulator. Before signing, the adjudicator submits the safety case to an adversarial audit tasked with falsifying its warrants. An **adversarial review**\index{Adversarial review!definition} is a structured audit that treats the safety case as an argument to be attacked rather than a brief for deployment. Confirmation bias steers the case's own data collection toward conditions where the learned models succeed, and the reviewer inverts that posture, searching for unsupported warrants, uncharacterized physical transitions, and edge conditions that break the release contract. An argument that fails on paper against an adversary trying to force a physical violation gives no reason to expect the machine to withstand service.

The review evaluates every evidentiary node in the argument tree with four probes. The first challenges **empirical sufficiency**\index{Empirical sufficiency}, whether the trials covered the physical extremes of the operating envelope. Stopping trials with the loaded base on dry concrete, at a friction near `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_dry_str`, support the warrant that the base reaches its credible deceleration there. The restricted mode, however, admits floors that the site's inspection regime certifies only to `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_inspected_str`, such as a lane polished by traffic, where the base may run at the restricted `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.v_restricted_str` that @sec-verification-operating-envelope declares, below the `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.v_inspected_ceiling_str` ceiling. If the trial set holds no loaded stops on such floors at that speed, the warrant for the restricted mode is unsupported, and a coverage audit finds in review the gap that service would otherwise find at a rack end. The reviewer also audits whether trials covered execution states of the newly flashed inactive software bank after activation, cold-start sensor characteristics before thermal stabilization, and canary fleet operating boundaries. The reviewer also challenges whether the site procedures actually exclude an oil film throughout the authorized interval. Listing oil outside the envelope does not establish that exclusion.

The second probe examines **domain transfer**\index{Domain transfer}, claims where simulation substitutes for hardware measurement\index{Simulation-to-reality leap}. A vision-based human detector may achieve high recall on synthetic, ray-traced warehouse environments, yet fail on physical hardware when encountering coworkers partially obscured by stretch-wrapped pallets whose specular reflections confound the camera's auto-exposure algorithm. Benchmark recall on curated offline datasets is an indirect proxy metric\index{Proxy metric fallacy} that scores isolated frames rather than the physical causal chain from detection to an arrested base. Likewise, a simulation that omits linkage compliance or fieldbus jitter cannot establish tolerance to those mechanisms; open-loop execution itself does not require either omission. The reviewer demands empirical evidence from paired hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) trials on target system-on-chip (SoC) devices connected to chassis dynamometers[^fn-chassis-dynamometer-rollers] and physical bus emulators under real facility illumination, dust, and reflective geometry.

[^fn-chassis-dynamometer-rollers]: **Chassis Dynamometer**\index{Dynamometer!chassis}: Powered rollers under the drive wheels absorb or supply torque, so the base can run at aisle speed on a bench while its drive and braking torques are measured. The rollers, not the floor, set the traction. Dynamometer stops can therefore qualify drive and brake response but say nothing about the friction premise of C3.

The third probe attacks **structural independence**\index{Structural independence}, asking whether the learned model and safety enforcer share hardware resources whose contention could delay sensor delivery or actuation cutoff. On modern robotics edge hardware where neural inference engines and real-time safety enforcers share a single system-on-chip die, internal crossbar interconnects, shared caches, and DRAM memory controllers, unconstrained direct memory access (DMA) transfers from large model forward passes can saturate memory channels. This memory contention induces tail latency spikes that starve deterministic safety enforcer execution ticks, invalidating the `{python} ReleaseClaims.t_age_str` observation-age chain of C4. Stress tests and timing analysis under peak synthetic compute and bus loads must establish the worst-case interference bound; unit tests on an otherwise idle bus provide zero evidence of non-interference. The reviewer also audits whether writing frozen edge telemetry ring buffers to non-volatile storage competes with real-time fieldbus DMA buffers across the internal bus fabric. The audit also checks for single points of failure in watchdog reset circuits and verifies whether the supercapacitor power hold-up circuit supplies sufficient energy to flush in-flight telemetry buffers to persistent flash when an emergency stop cuts main DC bus contactors.

The fourth probe identifies **unmonitored state drift**\index{Unmonitored state drift}. Mechanical wear alters gearbox compliance\index{Gearbox compliance}[^fn-strainwave-gear-wear] and disrupts the dynamic relationship between commanded motor torque and physical joint motion. The reviewer therefore demands paired wear-state braking and contact traces before accepting the arm-stop premise of the door branch of C1 (@sec-release-case-worked-full). A static motor-current threshold alone cannot prove that a mechanically worn drive train remains inside certified force and stopping limits. The reviewer also audits whether over-the-air updates preserve the persistent hardware calibration partition intact across schema migrations, or whether an OS reflash can silently reset camera extrinsics and joint zeroes to unverified factory defaults. The probe also checks whether thermal bracket motion remains inside the localization allowance; fresh timestamps and unchanged calibration files cannot establish that fact.

[^fn-strainwave-gear-wear]: **Strain-Wave Gear Wear**\index{Strain wave gearing!wear}: The arm's joints use strain-wave reducers (@sec-body-transmission-compliance), and in service their flexspline teeth and wave-generator bearing wear. Wear raises lost motion and torsional hysteresis, which adds phase lag between motor and link, so the arm begins to decelerate later and its first contact peak rises.

Reviewers operationalize these vulnerabilities by constructing explicit defeaters\index{Defeaters!adversarial review} for each warrant. The hardest to see combine minor anomalies that each stay inside their own bands, the compound faults that @sec-verification-deriving-fault-list derives from shared causes.

```{python}
#| label: calc-release-compound-defeater
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ DIAGNOSTIC THRESHOLDS IN THE COMPOUND DEFEATER
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-release-adversarial-review (compound-defeater paragraph).
# │ Goal: Hold the per-diagnostic thresholds that each anomaly stays inside.
# │ Show: the lens optical-transmission alarm threshold and the camera-mount
# │       deflection fault limit.
# │ How: chapter-local illustrative thresholds; no registry source exists. A
# │      site would take them from the camera's qualification and the mount's
# │      extrinsic-calibration tolerance analysis.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_percent, check

# ┌── 1. LOAD: chapter-local inputs ─────────────────────────────────────────────
optical_transmission_alarm = 0.85  # category: illustrative (lens transmission below which the check alarms; needs source)
mount_deflection_limit = 0.15 * ureg.degree  # category: illustrative (mount deflection fault limit; needs source)

# ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mount_deflection_limit_deg = mount_deflection_limit.to(ureg.degree).magnitude

# ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check(0 < optical_transmission_alarm < 1, "Transmission threshold is a fraction")
check(abs(mount_deflection_limit_deg - 0.15) < 1e-12, "Mount deflection limit 0.15 degree")

# ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class ReleaseCompoundDefeater:
    transmission_str = fmt_percent(optical_transmission_alarm, precision=0, style="prose")
    mount_limit_str = fmt(mount_deflection_limit_deg, precision=2)
```

Consider the mobile manipulator's navigation camera with a light film of dust on its lens, a mount that has shifted within tolerance after its fasteners relaxed and now shakes as the base crosses floor joints, and a harness whose flexing at those joints raises the error rate on its serializer/deserializer (SerDes) link. Each individual check reads normal: the optical transmission score exceeds its `{python} ReleaseCompoundDefeater.transmission_str` alarm threshold, the mount deflection registers below its `{python} ReleaseCompoundDefeater.mount_limit_str`-degree hardware fault limit, and SerDes cyclic redundancy check error counters\index{SerDes!link errors} remain below their alarm threshold. Their timing effects remain contained only if the independent permission path applies the event-specific age and clock-uncertainty checks of @sec-perception-observation-contract and retains its validated response. Interference that defeats that path is a C5 failure, not an availability-only event.

The same anomalies can combine in spatial estimation. Dimmed contrast reduces tracked features, mount vibration adds blur and pose bias, and frame drops extend intervals of dead reckoning. A pose bias can erode the localization allowance without forcing estimated covariance or innovation residuals to grow. The release reviewer therefore challenges the combined error against the qualified uncertainty bound, rather than inferring containment from individually passing scalar diagnostics. A failed combined bound consumes some of the stopping reserve and can invalidate the claim; exhausting the entire displayed reserve would require a quantified combined-error scenario. Residual monitoring is useful only for faults its qualification shows it can detect, with site restrictions or independent checks covering the remaining biases.

The review also audits the execution integrity of the permission path, whether inference or background services can bypass, corrupt, or starve the enforcer (@sec-enforcement) or human overrides (@sec-intervention), the latter covered by C6 of @tbl-16-cae-scorecard. Below the proposal boundary (@sec-boundary-machine-model), both keep non-preemptible priority over learned models, and the adversary asks whether a runaway policy thread, an accelerator-runtime exception, or a telemetry flood can saturate memory channels, lock a kernel spinlock, or brown out a rail. The reviewer accepts **permission path**\index{Permission path} independence, and the held-up rail that carries it on the mobile manipulator, only on physical fault injection, including bus saturation, feed removal, and a killed proposer task (F1), because C2 claims only the faults the permission path survives. Those trials are among the signed fault records of @sec-verification-fault-manifest. If the permission path is implemented in user-space software rather than isolated hard real-time threads and dedicated hardware interrupt lines, the reviewer marks the link as broken.

When an attack succeeds, the case cannot be salvaged by editing claim descriptions or inserting arbitrary margins. The broken warrant is traced to its systems failure, an uncharacterized physical boundary, an inadequate dataset, or an unmodeled latency, and the defect returns to the owning subsystem. A motor-current observer that fails under gearbox compliance returns to the mechanical specification as wear limits and runtime compliance estimation, and bus contention that delays the enforcer returns to the compute architecture as memory partitioning and real-time scheduling. The case returns to the engineering team with its broken warrants named, and only updated boundaries, re-derived stopping distances, and renewed verification reopen adjudication.

Review must also recur, because a case accepted once can erode in service without any single change that would force a new one. The *normalization of deviance*\index{Normalization of deviance} names that erosion, in which anomalies that cause no harm come to be read as acceptable operating noise rather than as evidence against a warrant [@leveson2011engineering; @vaughan1996challenger] (\ref{ws-release-challenger-experience-base-as-boundary}).[^fn-deviance-normalization-origin] On the mobile manipulator it would look like the compound defeater above spread over months: localization residuals that creep toward the edge of their tolerance, age refusals dismissed as nuisance stops, stops that end a little longer than the trials did, and enforcer trips cleared without a trace review. When thresholds are widened, margins trimmed for throughput, and alarms suppressed because nothing has yet gone wrong, the gap between the signed envelope and the machine's behavior widens until a routine disturbance exhausts what remains.

[^fn-deviance-normalization-origin]: **Normalization of Deviance**\index{Normalization of deviance!origin}: The sociologist Diane Vaughan coined the term in her study of the Challenger launch decision [@vaughan1996challenger]. It names a process rather than a decision, in which each anomaly that caused no harm widened what the next review accepted as normal. The countermeasure is therefore an indicator with a threshold fixed in advance, which a run of harmless readings cannot move.

::: {#ws-release-challenger-experience-base-as-boundary .callout-war-story title="Challenger and experience limits (1986)"}
**Context**: The Space Shuttle's solid rocket motors were assembled from segments whose field joints were sealed by a primary and a secondary O-ring [@rogers1986challenger]. No learned model appears in this chain. The adjudication failure it records is the one this chapter's verdicts exist to prevent, a launch approved for conditions that the evidence did not cover.

**Mechanism**: The ambient temperature at launch was $36^\circ\text{F}$, 15 degrees colder than any previous launch. O-ring resiliency falls with temperature, and a cold ring returns to shape too slowly to follow the joint gap as ignition pressure opens it. On the eve of launch, engineers at Morton Thiokol, the motor's contractor, recommended against launching below $53^\circ\text{F}$, the O-ring temperature of the coldest previous flight, whose joints had shown the worst blow-by to date. That limit was the edge of flight experience, not a qualified bound. NASA managers countered with a qualification temperature that applied to the propellant's bulk temperature rather than to the seals.

**Impact**: A combustion gas leak through the right booster's aft field joint, beginning at or shortly after ignition, weakened or penetrated the External Tank. The vehicle broke up about 73 seconds after launch, and all seven crew members died.

**Response**: The Commission attributed the failure to "a faulty design unacceptably sensitive to a number of factors," and temperature heads its list of those factors. It recommended that the joint be changed and that the new design be certified by tests "over the full range of operating conditions, including temperature."

**Systems lesson**: Thiokol management reversed its engineers' recommendation at the urging of NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center. Thiokol's vice president of engineering testified, "We had to prove to them that we weren't ready." The burden of proof had moved from showing the joint safe inside its evidence to showing it unsafe outside the evidence, where no data existed. The Commission also found that O-ring erosion had recurred on earlier flights and that NASA and Thiokol "accepted escalating risk apparently because they 'got away with it last time'" [@rogers1986challenger], so the flight record itself had been read as evidence of safety. A release verdict keeps the burden where the envelope trichotomy puts it. A condition outside the evidence, such as a seal temperature below all flight experience, is unknown, and the verdict refuses it.
:::

Tempe's takeover premise (@sec-boundary-when-fails) was a condition of the same kind, and @sec-intervention-failure-modes posed the operator-monitoring question it raises. A release that relies on such a premise must bind its response, refusal or a restricted case, together with its tested physical limits.

A case that survives adversarial review has had its warrants attacked, but its verdict still lives only on paper. The release manifest turns the surviving argument and the verdict it supports into a record that the machine itself checks before it moves.

## The Release Manifest {#sec-release-manifest}

A release verdict is formally codified in the **release manifest** (\ref{dfn-release-safety-case-dossier}), the fourteenth record in the record chain. The manifest seals the Goal Structuring Notation assurance argument and the signed operational design domain invariants together with the evidence they rest on. It is the immutable wire-level artifact that binds the fault records to the signed verdict of the lead systems adjudicator and refuses motion whenever the running images, hardware attestation, or empirical evidence no longer match its digests.[^fn-hw-crypto-manifest]

The release manifest connects the engineering decisions made throughout the book. Each upstream record states a boundary or supplies evidence that the release argument must evaluate; recording or signing it does not by itself establish the claim. The manifest binds the reviewed versions of these records into the argument graph:

1. **Physical plant and timing base:** The kinodynamic limit record (@sec-body-actuator-limits) recording torque, velocity, and thermal bounds with their supporting evidence; the proposer's payload requirements (@sec-brain-action-chunking) specifying candidate action horizons, which enter the handoff record rather than forming a record of their own; and the handoff record (@sec-nervous-deterministic-fieldbuses) recording fieldbus jitter and communication deadlines with their qualification premises.
2. **Data, policy, and behavioral bounds:** The demonstration provenance record (@sec-data-schema) recording dataset calibrations and operating-domain coverage; the policy manifest (@sec-training-policy-manifest) binding neural network weights and the properties actually established for that candidate; and the evaluation record (@sec-evaluation-logs) reporting closed-loop task performance, interventions, and evaluated conditions.
3. **Perception, belief, and planning:** The observation contract (@sec-perception-observation-contract) carrying observation-age and synchronization bounds; the spatial belief record (@sec-memory-handoff) carrying spatial estimates, uncertainty, and validity conditions; the intent lease (@sec-intent-handoff) recording the grounded goal and tolerances; and the trajectory record (@sec-planning-trajectory-contract) carrying the motion, seam conditions, deadlines, and stopping continuation for validation.
4. **Deterministic containment, execution, and verification:** The enforcement record (@sec-enforcement-admitted-command-schema), whose admitted commands report the runtime command selected by the enforcer, distinct from the signed enforcement contract that configures its barriers and fallback rules; the placement record (@sec-placement-hardware-allocation) recording resource allocation and qualification premises; the authority record (@sec-intervention-authority-log) recording authority-transfer decisions and outcomes; and the fault records (@sec-verification-fault-manifest) recording tested coverage and unresolved gaps.

To these upstream contracts, the release manifest adds the claim root, the GSN argument digest, binary image hashes (covering neural weights, the enforcer's logic in both nominal and restricted configurations, and the real-time kernel), sensor calibration references, the adjudicator's signed verdict, non-negotiable standing conditions, a lifecycle wear budget of operating hours and cycles, and a calendar expiry. Evidence links must resolve to these exact reviewed record digests, committed under one evidence root in the manner of a hash tree [@merkle1988digital], before hardware root-of-trust gates permit motor power stages to energize.

::: {#dfn-release-safety-case-dossier .callout-definition title="Release manifest"}

***Release manifest***\index{Release manifest!definition}\index{Release contract!release manifest} is the signed, tamper-evident record binding all upstream physical AI engineering records into an immutable operational release claim, consisting of the Goal Structuring Notation argument graph, operational design domain invariants, standing conditions, and the digests and signed verdict that seal them.

1.  **Significance**: Functions as the capstone release contract of the physical AI architecture, establishing legal and physical custody across the Brain's policy weights and evaluation records, the Nervous System's deterministic timing budgets, the Body's kinodynamic limits, and the fault records of verification.
2.  **Distinction**: Unlike static software release notes, an empirical test summary, or an advisory compliance certificate, a release manifest binds high-level operational claims to concrete empirical evidence, enforces hardware root-of-trust attestation, and mandates non-negotiable standing conditions that withdraw tracking within the qualified detection and response budget when evidence expires.
3.  **Common pitfall**: Treating the release manifest as a retrospective administrative artifact assembled for regulatory sign-off, rather than a living cyber-physical contract whose digests and standing conditions are actively validated by real-time safety monitors before energizing motor windings.

:::

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ **Byte layout:** The release manifest's fields, types, and digests are given in @sec-appendix-systems-wire-release.

[^fn-hw-crypto-manifest]: **Cryptographic Manifest and Silicon Attestation**\index{Cryptographic manifest!hardware Root of Trust}: One-time programmable electronic fuses (OTP/eFuse) hold the adjudicator's public verification key, so no software update can replace it. Secure bootstrap verifies each boot stage before passing it control [@arbaugh1997secure], and measured boot extends each stage's measurement into Trusted Platform Module Platform Configuration Registers (TPM PCRs), which the verifier compares with the measurements the signed manifest expects. An image the key did not sign therefore never reaches the permit.

@Fig-16-release-record places authentication and physical standing checks before an operating permit. The gate first authenticates the manifest, images, and complete reviewed evidence set, then checks current calibration, maintenance, and site conditions. Only a matching case can enable the plant's assessed startup sequence; the protocol and canonical fields are collected in @sec-appendix-systems-release-protocol and @sec-appendix-systems-wire-release. During motion, a failed condition commands the assessed fallback before a bank change or power isolation.

|:-------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|

| `COND`                   | All restricted evidence valid and current                                                 | Included if calibration stale              | Signed restricted envelope under enforcer; `COND` |
