Every evidence leaf needs an identifier for its raw trace, instrument, calibration, configuration, and test script. A measured timing tail enters as a percentile, and a hard response claim needs the separately justified bound of @sec-nervous-deterministic-fieldbuses. The coworker's handover criterion needs load-cell time series for the specified body-region surrogate and geometry. Linked records let an auditor repeat the test and identify where the claim stops applying.

The release manifest names the configuration and physical limits for which its verdict applies. A changed policy weight file, real-time priority, driver, or unverified component revision requires a new case or an explicitly approved equivalent. For the mobile manipulator, the signed wear limits on joint backlash and brake lining thickness come from measured stopping and load evidence. Refusal conditions of the operating envelope include a tote-rack load above its capacity, which the rack load cells monitor, and an unsurveyed floor, which the site procedure enforces (@tbl-16-odd-invariants). The manifest also signs the permission path's isolated, held-up rail as a standing condition, sized in @sec-enforcement-fallback-ladder, with a capacity self-test of its hold-up store gating the permit at every power-up. When a measured condition crosses a signed limit, the permission path revokes tracking at its specified detection and response time and commands the assessed fallback.

The manifest must bind event records to the configuration that produced them. Local traces and fleet summaries serve different purposes: the former reconstruct a boundary excursion, while the latter reveal recurring drift. The capture and curation mechanisms of @sec-release-data-curation-flywheel must preserve that provenance when they supply evidence for a revised case.

Field telemetry records torque residuals, loop timing, and enforcer trips for drift review, while the permission path checks the signed live thresholds at the cadence the plant requires. A brake response measured at scheduled inspection beyond the signed clearance budget, or stale calibration, revokes the current verdict, and reinstalling an earlier signed image cannot restore worn brakes. Unless a separately signed `COND` case covers that physical state, the plant uses its assessed stop and awaits maintenance and re-adjudication (@tbl-16-release-authorization).

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The premises a release manifest leaves open become entries in the residual-claims register of @sec-frontier-residual-claims-register.
:::

The warehouse response ends with the base supported at rest. Another plant may need continuing powered support, as a machine that falls when torque is removed illustrates (\ref{capstone-release-humanoid-crucible}).

::: {#capstone-release-humanoid-crucible .callout-perspective title="When removing torque causes the harm"}
**Question**: Which verdict applies when removing torque causes the harm?

A supported base at rest has removed its translational kinetic hazard, while an upright humanoid can retain a gravitational fall hazard. Before standing, a refusal can keep the machine in its supported rest state. Once it is upright, withdrawing walking authority requires a validated arrest or support response.

* **Torque removal can cause a fall.** An unsupported upright biped with backdrivable joints can collapse when motor torque is removed (@sec-nervous-actuation-authority). That plant cannot use torque removal as its assessed stop unless a qualified passive support or arrest mechanism prevents the fall.
* **The fall-arrest response is itself an actuation.** Crouching, stepping, or lowering the robot to the floor under power is a commanded motion that needs its own claim, its own evidence, and a place in the fault set. A `REFUSE` verdict still depends on the part of the machine that keeps it standing.
* **Wear revokes the running permit.** Sole friction and joint backlash drift out of the limits the fall-arrest evidence assumed, and crossing a signed wear limit withdraws the permit to walk before the arrest response that the permit relies on stops working.
:::

::: {#chk-release-student-verdict .callout-checkpoint title="Deriving a verdict from your own measurements"}

@Tbl-16-cond-measurements carries no measured values, because this book has none. Fill it with values of your own, from trials on a machine you can test or from numbers you choose, and derive the verdict they support:

- [ ] **Graded values**: For each row, record your value and its source, and grade the premise measured, datasheet, illustrative, or unknown. A number you choose grades illustrative, and a manufacturer's rated value grades datasheet; measured means your own trial or a published measurement you cite.
- [ ] **Verdict derivation**: A `COND` case requires adequate support for every relied-on premise: qualified measurements, justified analysis, or validated operating restrictions. Illustrative values alone still support only an actual `REFUSE`. Recompute the base's budget and spare from your values. If every relied-on premise has adequate support, name the envelope the `COND` case signs and the premise that keeps the normal mode unsigned. If a relied-on premise lacks adequate support, derive the verdict the table *would* support given the missing evidence, and label that verdict hypothetical.
- [ ] **Artifact label**: Mark the filled table as your own work, whose values license no machine.
:::

The release manifest closes the release decision for a particular configuration. Updating that configuration reopens the relevant claims, so the deployment process must preserve the same relation between evidence and authority.

## Maintaining Release Through Updates {#sec-release-deployment-lifecycle}

Continuing the stipulated branch, suppose the restricted mug-delivery policy is retrained to reduce hesitation at the controlled pick station. That candidate must return through the release decision before it can command the warehouse machine. The signed case provides the basis for deciding which evidence can be reused, which tests must be repeated, and how the machine remains controlled during the update. Deployment mechanisms serve that decision by preserving the reviewed configuration and recording evidence for the next one.

### Modular safety cases and continuous over-the-air deployment {#sec-release-modular-safety-cases}

The retrained policy changes the capability evidence directly. It can also change accelerator load, observation delivery, or proposed contact motions, so the reviewer traces those dependencies before deciding which containment records remain applicable. **Over-the-air (OTA) updates**\index{Over-the-air update!safety case decomposition}\index{Modular safety case!continuous deployment} change a named configuration; **modular safety cases**\index{Safety case!modular GSN decomposition}, whose claims record the evidence and configuration they depend on, identify which claims that change reopens [@denney2015dynamic].

The containment argument covers the measured plant, sensor bounds, timing, and independent permission path. Its premises include the tracking error tube $\epsilon_{\text{track}}$ (@sec-enforcement-handoff), stopping budget (@sec-nervous-coupled-budget), contact passivity barrier (@sec-enforcement-intentional-contact), and watchdog response. Evidence for these claims can be reused only if the update preserves the conditions under which it was obtained. A larger model can change contention or power demand without changing safety-filter source code, so an unchanged enforcer binary does not establish an unchanged containment argument. Its protection remains limited to the observed hazards and validated responses within $\mathcal{C}_{\text{viable}}$.

The capability argument establishes useful task behavior within the declared operating domain. Candidate evaluation, shadow traces, and restricted closed-loop trials test whether a new policy improves that behavior. A refusal or stop can contain a rejected proposal under the validated assumptions, but frequent refusals may make the service unusable. Release therefore reviews capability and containment together, retaining evidence only where the changed configuration leaves its supporting premises intact.

The update mechanism must preserve the same configuration boundary. **Dual A/B OS partitioning**\index{Dual A/B OS partitioning!OTA architecture}\index{Atomic update!operating system} writes a candidate to an inactive bank while retaining the reviewed image. Activating the candidate requires an assessed stationary update state: the body and payload remain supported, sufficient energy remains for restart and testing, and the permission path prevents tracking during cutover. The rollback decision is governed by @sec-release-verdicts-ota-watchdogs. A signature on the image is not enough if one stolen key can sign any image for the whole fleet. Secure update frameworks therefore split signing among separate roles held under separate keys, so that compromising one key does not let an attacker install an image; The Update Framework introduced the design and Uptane adapts it to vehicles, whose many controllers each receive their own images [@samuel2010survivable; @kuppusamy2016uptane].

**Persistent hardware calibration parameter retention**\index{Hardware calibration!persistent parameter retention}\index{Parameter partition!decoupled storage} prevents the **calibration clashing failure**\index{Calibration clashing failure}, in which a software replacement overwrites the machine's measured parameters. Camera intrinsics ($K$), sensor transforms ($[R \mid t]$), joint offsets, and motor torque constants ($K_\tau$) belong to the individual machine and may change through calibration or wear. A protected parameter store separates them from the replaceable OS banks. Schema migration writes a new version while retaining the old image's compatible record, so rollback restores an image-record pair. A valid checksum establishes record integrity; current physical checks establish whether the calibration still applies.

**Forensic traceability**\index{Forensic traceability!release provenance}\index{Release manifest!cryptographic provenance} connects each deployed image to its training provenance, calibration records, and reviewed test results in the signed manifest (@sec-release-manifest). After an intervention, these links identify which configuration produced the trace and which warrants must be reconsidered. A digest establishes identity; identifying the physical cause still requires evidence and analysis.

### Staging candidate policies before release {#sec-release-candidate-staging}

A candidate must repeat the **hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) regression gates**\index{Hardware-in-the-loop!regression gates}\index{Release engineering!HIL regression testing} affected by its changes. Software simulation represents timing and electrical effects only where its models include them; a target-hardware bench exercises the actual processors, communication links, and drives. The bench must expose the interference and fault mechanisms on which the release claims depend:

1. **Worst-case execution time (WCET) and scheduling jitter**: Profiling whether neural forward passes and safety filter evaluations complete within hard real-time deadlines ($T_{\text{exec}} \le T_{\text{deadline}}$) under peak memory bus crossbar contention and simultaneous DMA transfers (@sec-placement-isolation-decisions).
2. **Deterministic bus arbitration**: Measuring fieldbus communication jitter and cyclic transmission integrity across physical EtherCAT or CAN-FD networks under simulated telemetry broadcast floods and electrical noise injection.
3. **Power-stage thermal dynamics and current ripple**: Verifying that high-frequency control chatter or torque ripple proposed by the candidate policy does not induce excessive inverter switching losses, DC rail voltage sag, or thermal runaway in motor windings (@sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles).
4. **Hardware fault-injection survivability**: Validating that physical line breaks, power supply brownouts, or deserializer frame dropouts deterministically trigger the hardware watchdog and safe-stop sequence within certified timing budgets before motor power stages can be damaged.

A candidate advances only when its required tests pass and the records support the stated timing and physical bounds. Observing no deadline overrun in a finite campaign does not by itself establish a worst-case bound.

In cloud software engineering, blue-green deployment achieves zero downtime by spinning up an identical green cluster and instantly flipping a virtual IP or DNS CNAME record. In physical AI, however, blue-green cutover cannot be executed instantaneously while mass is in motion. Swapping active control authority between an incumbent controller and a candidate policy mid-stride or at speed requires managing actuator state continuity, motor winding back-EMF, and dynamic tracking tubes (@sec-intervention-authority-transitions); de-energizing motor windings or inducing sudden torque steps introduces severe mechanical shock loads ($N^2 J \ddot{\theta}$) and loss of traction. An unvalidated policy also cannot simply be granted partial motor authority in a populated warehouse to "canary test" edge-case performance.

Safe predeployment staging instead relies on **shadow mode deployment**\index{Shadow mode deployment!definition}. The incumbent controller $\pi_{\text{incumbent}}$ supplies proposals, while the independent enforcer retains sole actuator-output ownership and checks each command before fieldbus dispatch. Concurrently in the background, the candidate neural policy $\pi_{\text{candidate}}$ executes on the host compute SoC, consuming identical live sensor streams $s_t$ within its qualified shared-resource budget and computing what control command $u_t^{\text{cand}} \sim \pi_{\text{candidate}}(s_t)$ it would have proposed. The candidate writes its outputs to an isolated telemetry buffer that grants no actuator authority. Consumers can read that record, but neither the buffer nor the candidate can bypass the enforcer. Shadow inference and recording must stay within the interference and power budgets that preserve the active case. Discrepancies between candidate proposals and the incumbent's admitted commands are logged as high-rate telemetry events without admitting any candidate command to the drives.

Shadow-mode telemetry monitors two instantaneous divergence metrics:

1. **Action discrepancy** ($\Delta u_t$): The Euclidean or angular distance between the candidate proposal and the incumbent control action:
   $$\Delta u_t = \| u_t^{\text{cand}} - u_t^{\text{incumbent}} \|_2.$$
   Sustained spikes in $\Delta u_t$ identify behavioral divergence where the candidate policy exhibits unmodeled bias, high-frequency control jitter, or erratic steering commands. In addition, the discrepancy analyzer monitors the command-rate norm $\|\dot{u}_t^{\text{cand}}\|_2$, which is a torque-rate norm only when $u$ is a torque command, to detect unmodeled control chatter that would excite mechanical resonances.

2. **Safety barrier margin discrepancy** ($\Delta B_t$): The differential proximity to forward-invariant safety boundaries under a control barrier function $h(x)$ (@sec-enforcement-safe-sets-conditional-permission):
   $$\Delta B_t = \dot{h}(\hat{x}_t, u_t^{\text{cand}}) - \dot{h}(\hat{x}_t, u_t^{\text{incumbent}}),$$
   where $\hat{x}_t$ is the state estimated from the sensor streams $s_t$.
   A negative $\Delta B_t$ means the candidate has a smaller modeled barrier derivative than the incumbent. Both derivatives can still be positive, so the sign alone does not imply decreasing clearance or a violated boundary of $\mathcal{C}_{\text{viable}}$ (defined by $h(x) \ge 0$).

The two discrepancies answer different questions. A large $\Delta u_t$ can reflect an alternate useful action, while $\Delta B_t$ indicates how the proposals differ in their modeled effect on the barrier. Neither sign alone supplies a verdict: review must consider the current margin, uncertainty, and the condition that the independent enforcer would require.

Shadow mode nevertheless meets a limit that more traces cannot remove, **counterfactual divergence**\index{Counterfactual divergence!shadow mode}\index{Covariate shift!open-loop replay}. Because admitted incumbent proposals determine the plant trajectory, the historical state trajectory $\tau = (s_0, u_0^{\text{inc}}, s_1, u_1^{\text{inc}}, \dots)$ is conditioned entirely on incumbent actions. The candidate policy operates open-loop; its proposed actions $u_t^{\text{cand}}$ never alter the physical environment, induce vehicle motion, or trigger real-time sensor feedback. Conflating open-loop agreement with deployment safety is the **open-loop replay fallacy**\index{Open-loop replay fallacy}: assuming that high action agreement during passive trace replay guarantees closed-loop dynamic stability. The $O(T^2 \epsilon)$ result in @sec-data-endogenous-experience is an expected-cost bound under its stated imitation-learning assumptions, not a universal law for physical tracking error. A candidate that agrees on incumbent trajectories can still visit unfamiliar states or excite unmodeled dynamics when it closes the loop, the covariate shift that interactive imitation learning was designed to correct [@ross2011reduction]. Shadow mode is an essential pre-filter for gross behavioral anomalies, but never a substitute for closed-loop dynamic qualification.

**Phased canary fleet rollouts**\index{Canary deployment!physical AI fleet}\index{Release engineering!canary rollouts}[^fn-canary-miners-origin] expose the candidate to closed-loop operation under a separately supported restricted case. Selecting fewer machines limits exposure but does not bound the consequence of any one action. The restrictions must address the physical hazard:

1. **Geofenced operational containment**: Canary units operate exclusively within dedicated, surveyed low-risk corridors, such as wide transit aisles devoid of blind rack corners, reduced pedestrian density, and high-friction surveyed concrete ($\mu \ge$ `{python} ReleaseEnvelope.mu_dry_str`).
2. **Enforced kinematic derating**: The real-time safety enforcer clamps candidate policy velocity and acceleration below nominal ratings ($v \le v_{\text{canary}} < v_{\text{nominal}}$), expanding stopping distance margins and suppressing transient kinetic energy.
3. **Supervised human oversight**: High-readiness human supervisors equipped with wireless remote emergency-stop (tele-stop) pendants maintain line-of-sight monitoring over canary units, backed by an active-lease watchdog.
4. **Targeted regression observability**: The trial measures tracking error variance $\sigma_{\text{track}}^2$, drive torque ripple, and enforcer intervention frequency to reveal service regressions. The permission path retains only the containment claims validated for the restricted envelope.

[^fn-canary-miners-origin]: **Canary**\index{Canary deployment!etymology} (the miners' sentinel bird): Miners carried caged canaries because the birds succumb to carbon monoxide before people do, so a bird's distress warned the crew to leave. The metaphor carries this section's warning. The canary is the unit exposed to the hazard first, so on a physical fleet its exposure must be bounded by containment, not by how few units are chosen.

Expansion requires predeclared acceptance criteria tied to the service and physical claims. Intervention-rate non-inferiority,[^fn-noninferiority-canary-margin] with a margin $\delta$ fixed before the trial so that the upper one-sided 95 percent confidence bound on the rate ratio $\lambda_{\text{canary}}/\lambda_{\text{incumbent}}$ must fall below $1+\delta$, and tracking variance $\sigma_{\text{track}}^2 \le \sigma_{\text{incumbent}}^2$ are possible capability criteria, with their comparison conditions and statistical assumptions stated. Without the margin, the criterion becomes a demand to prove the candidate better, which the small exposure of a canary can almost never satisfy; the exposure arithmetic of @sec-evaluation-trial-limits sets how much operation a given $\delta$ requires, and a sequential test (@sec-evaluation-sequential-sprt) can stop expansion as soon as the evidence suffices. None of these criteria replaces the evidence for stopping, observation, or containment. An enforcer intervention also needs causal review: suppressing legitimate clamps to improve a rollout metric would weaken the release argument.

[^fn-noninferiority-canary-margin]: **Non-Inferiority Testing**\index{Non-inferiority test!canary rollout}: The design comes from clinical trials, where failing to find a difference proves nothing, so a new treatment must instead be shown worse than the standard by no more than a margin fixed before any data arrive [@blackwelder1982proving]. A canary can therefore pass on modest exposure without proving the candidate better, but only if $\delta$ was not chosen after the result was seen.

### From qualification to a new manifest {#sec-release-ota-staging}

For the retrained mug-delivery candidate, the reviewer repeats closed-loop capability evaluation under the restricted route and feed conditions, and repeats the loaded timing and fault tests whose dependencies changed. Unaffected plant evidence remains reusable only while configuration, calibration, wear, and site premises still match. A reduced hesitation rate does not justify relaxing contact or floor restrictions.

Assume, still within the stipulated branch, that those results satisfy the predeclared capability criteria and preserve the containment claims. The adjudicator issues a new manifest binding the candidate, retained and repeated evidence, current calibration, and the same restricted mission. At the assessed stationary cutover state, the gate authenticates that manifest and checks current standing conditions before admitting new proposals. Field monitoring then compares the running service with the same success, cycle-time, rescue, and protection criteria. Failed qualification leaves the incumbent case unchanged; a failed standing condition withdraws the affected grant.

### Over-the-air staging and watchdog-enforced rollbacks {#sec-release-verdicts-ota-watchdogs}

A candidate written to the inactive bank inherits no operating grant from its predecessor. **Hardware watchdog rollback triggers**\index{Watchdog rollback!hardware triggers}\index{Hardware watchdog!OTA rollback} must distinguish failure to boot from failure during motion. Before tracking is enabled, failed image authentication, startup tests, or fieldbus synchronization can reject the candidate and select the retained image. That image must still pass current calibration and standing-condition checks; rollback cannot repair the physical plant.

During motion, the independent supervisor first commands the assessed fallback within its measured response budget. Where that response ends in torque removal, the supervisor asserts Safe Torque Off after the required controlled stop; a plant needing a powered hold retains the authority needed for that hold. A missed enforcer heartbeat therefore withdraws tracking permission without making software restart the stopping mechanism. Only after the plant reaches its validated update state may the boot selector change banks.

The image and its compatible calibration schema form the rollback unit. If either record is missing, corrupted, or physically stale, the gate selects `REFUSE` unless a separately signed restricted case covers the actual state and its limits, such as $v \le v_{\text{restricted}}$. Keeping the previous binary supplies a recovery option, not evidence that the old verdict still applies.

### Fleet telematics and the closed-loop data curation flywheel {#sec-release-data-curation-flywheel}

An enforcer trip can reveal a policy failure, a changed physical premise, or both. The field record must let the reviewer distinguish those causes before choosing retraining, maintenance, or a narrower envelope. Wireless summaries alone cannot reconstruct the observations and actuator response around the event, so detailed traces are retained locally.

**Edge event-triggered telemetry**\index{Edge event-triggered telemetry!architecture} retains the sensor, proposal, permission, actuator, and timestamp chain around an intervention or boundary excursion. A local rolling buffer preserves the lead-up; capture continues through the physical response when the qualified recording power path survives. Buffer length, write bandwidth, and hold-up energy are sized from the required reconstruction window and verified under the same contention and power faults as the permission path. A logic-rail capacitor does not guarantee that the full sensor and storage path survives, and recording must never delay the stop.

UL 4600 calls the field measurements that keep a claim alive **safety performance indicators**\index{Safety performance indicator} (SPIs). Each is a metric tied to a named claim, with a threshold and a predeclared response when the threshold is crossed [@ul4600]. On the running machine, every standing condition of @sec-release-standing-conditions has one. Measured stop distance at scheduled trials and enforcer trips per operating hour watch the base's stopping claim, age refusals per operating hour watch the observation-age claim, and localization residuals against their allowance watch the sensor geometry. An SPI whose threshold is crossed withdraws or narrows the grant it watches; one that drifts toward its threshold triggers review before it is crossed, which is the defense against the normalization of deviance of @sec-release-adversarial-review.

Compact health summaries support fleet monitoring, while required incident records retain full provenance locally until transfer succeeds. Learning-data filters may prioritize unfamiliar events, but cannot discard required safety evidence or hide repeated failures. A reviewer distinguishes policy hesitation from calibration drift, contamination, and mechanism wear before assigning the repair. Qualified recovery traces can enter the experience pipeline of @sec-data-schema; reconstructed simulations extend test coverage only over their modeled conditions.

A captured event changes the release argument only after its cause and conditions are established. Reconstructed scenes and retraining can improve a candidate, but neither automatically repairs a physical warrant. The revised claim must return through the relevant qualification stages before a new manifest grants authority.

### Recorded people as a standing condition {#sec-release-recorded-people}

Every record this release relies on also records people. The authority log of @sec-intervention-authority-log names the operator behind each takeover, tick by tick. The event-triggered traces above hold camera frames of whoever stood in the aisle, workers who never touched the console among them, and the demonstration archive of @sec-data-schema binds each episode to the operator who produced it. None of that evidence can be discarded without weakening the incident reconstruction that the release depends on, and none of it is only about the machine. The release therefore carries one more premise, and it is administrative rather than physical: each record that identifies a person declares its purpose, its retention period, and who may read it, and the site operates within those declarations.

Where the machine runs in the European Union, the General Data Protection Regulation makes that premise law [@gdpr2016]. Article 5(1) requires personal data to be collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with them (point b), to be limited to what those purposes need (point c), and to be kept in identifiable form no longer than they require (point e). Article 25(2) makes the minimum the default, in the amount collected, the extent of processing, the storage period, and accessibility. Article 35 requires a data protection impact assessment before processing that is likely to result in a high risk to the people concerned, and Article 88 lets member states and collective agreements set more specific rules for employee data, naming monitoring systems at the workplace among the safeguards those rules must address. Other jurisdictions differ in detail; the engineering premise does not.

Each declaration becomes a standing condition of the kind @sec-release-standing-conditions defines, with a detector and a response. Incident reconstruction sets the retention of the black-box and authority logs: the traces around an intervention are kept until the event's review closes, and routine ticks with no event roll off the ring buffer as they already do. Access follows the purpose, so an incident reviewer may read a trace and an operator's supervisor may not score from it. A trace promoted into the experience pipeline carries its purpose and retention with it, which is what the consent and retention field of @tbl-05-provenance-schema records. The detector is an access and retention audit on the evidence store; its response follows from the rule that a verdict stands only while its premises are known-true, so a record used outside its declared purpose, or held past its period, suspends that use and returns the premise to the adjudicator. Stating the premise this way keeps the record chain honest in both directions. It must not lose the evidence a stop needs, and it must not become a surveillance record that no release decision ever authorized.

### Fleet evidence and accountable release {#sec-release-fleet-exposure-liability}

Fleet exposure can reveal recurring failures, but its interpretation requires the operating domain, intervention definition, and configuration. Pooling dissimilar routes or treating an intervention count as a collision rate breaks the warrant. The release reviewer uses fleet records to challenge the same capability and containment claims, rather than replacing them with a mileage ranking.

The signed release manifest records the engineering decision and its accountable owner. It does not itself establish regulatory compliance or determine legal liability. Applicable requirements depend on the machine, intended use, and jurisdiction; the release manifest must preserve the evidence needed for that separate assessment.

The Cruise robotaxi collision of October 2023 shows what happens when that evidence is not preserved and disclosed (\ref{ws-data-cruise-robotaxi-pedestrian-drag-2023-missing}). After a human-driven car threw a pedestrian into its path, the driverless vehicle stopped, then attempted to pull over and dragged her beneath it. The engineering failure was a post-collision classification error. The release failure came afterward. Cruise's crash reports to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) omitted the dragging, and a video shown to the agency the next morning stopped before it [@doj2024cruise]. On 24 October 2023 the California Department of Motor Vehicles suspended Cruise's deployment and driverless testing permits, citing among its grounds that the company had misrepresented information related to the safety of its autonomous technology [@cadmv2023cruise]. In September 2024 NHTSA imposed a consent order with a \$1.5 million penalty for incomplete crash reports [@nhtsa2024cruiseconsent], and in November 2024 Cruise entered a deferred prosecution agreement and paid a \$500,000 criminal fine for a false record submitted to influence the federal investigation [@doj2024cruise]. Regulators withdrew the operating authority not only because of what the vehicle did but because the record of its behavior did not reach them. A release manifest that binds raw traces to the configuration that produced them, and that an assessor can open, is the engineering counterpart of that obligation.

Release remains a decision about a named machine under named conditions throughout this lifecycle. Shadow traces, staged trials, and field records can strengthen the next argument only when their operating conditions and limits are explicit; the manifest and independent permission path retain the restrictions that the evidence supports.

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-release-fallacies-pitfalls}

Adjudicating the release of physical AI systems requires exposing unstated assumptions before kinetic energy is transferred to mass. The following fallacies and pitfalls highlight common misattributions between software confidence and cyber-physical reality.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Statistical coverage substitutes for deterministic architectural warrants.*

A team presents millions of simulated hours and thousands of incident-free cycles as its release argument. The record supplies evidence about the tested conditions, but demonstrating the catastrophic failure rate\index{Failure rate!catastrophic} a release claim names can require more physical exposure than any schedule allows (@sec-evaluation-trial-limits). Simulation also retains the assumptions of its physical models, such as idealized Coulomb friction or infinitely rigid gearboxes. The release case must explain how architectural enforcement\index{Architectural warrants}, such as an independent permission path that revokes motion and commands a validated stop, constrains harmful policy behavior, and it must provide evidence for that mechanism under its stated assumptions. Empirical performance and architectural warrants answer different questions; a large trial count cannot replace the missing argument that connects actuator authority\index{Actuator authority} to physical limits.

**Exposure can bound a hazard rate under its sampling and event-model assumptions; infeasible exposure targets and omitted faults limit that warrant.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Couple policy evaluation with independently qualified enforcement. State the observed hazards, plant bounds, timing, and fallback premises under which the invariant claim holds.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *A release verdict is a permanent certification of safety.*

A machine passes validation and enters production under a signed safety case\index{Safety case!lifecycle}. Over time, brake pad wear lengthens stopping distances, kinematic calibration drifts due to thermal cycling, and optical contamination degrades sensing. The software can remain unchanged while the physical assumptions supporting the release fail. The release manifest needs maintenance requirements and invalidation triggers\index{Invalidation triggers} tied to relevant lifecycle counters or measured drift, with defined restrictions when those conditions fail. A signature records responsibility for a bounded release decision; it does not make the tested body's hardware capabilities permanent.

**Software bit-exactness does not prevent physical mechanical and tribological decay.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Enforce perishable release manifests with mandatory operating-hour, calendar-age, and mechanical-cycle limits. Require verified recalibration self-tests at power-up before motor power stages are energized.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Relying on unstated environmental assumptions to support a safety claim.*

A team verifies the base's stopping performance in well-lit aisles on clean floors, and its case states the floor's friction but never its lighting. A dim aisle then costs service through the image age that a runtime check happens to see (@sec-release-safety-cases-claims) and costs clearance through weaker feature matches whose localization error no check sees, against an allowance the well-lit trials sized (@sec-release-adversarial-review). The mechanical brake\index{Brake!mechanical} performs exactly as tested and every diagnostic reads normal while the spare in the stopping distance\index{Stopping distance} shrinks. The safety case must state the environmental conditions on which its claims depend and explain how operation remains within them. Where monitoring can detect a violation, it must trigger the defined restriction or fallback; an unstated assumption supplies neither a testable release condition nor a usable runtime boundary.

**Unstated operating assumptions silently erode safety margins until an ordinary disturbance causes a collision.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Formally enumerate every environmental parameter (ambient lux, floor friction, thermal range) as a monitored premise in the release manifest. Pair each premise with a deterministic runtime detector or a mandatory site operating regime.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Shadow-mode qualification guarantees closed-loop dynamic stability.*

A candidate neural policy is evaluated in shadow mode across thousands of fleet operating hours, demonstrating negligible action discrepancy ($\Delta u_t \approx 0$) relative to the incumbent controller released under the signed case. The team assumes that this high behavioral fidelity proves the candidate policy is ready for full autonomous release. Because the incumbent controller commands the plant, the historical state trajectory remains entirely on the distribution induced by the incumbent. The candidate policy never experiences the physical consequences of its own actions. A candidate policy that appears benign in open-loop replay can suffer compounding tracking errors, high-frequency limit cycles, or actuator chattering the moment it closes the control loop.

**Open-loop trace replay masks covariate shift and unmodeled actuator-plant resonances.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Treat shadow mode as a necessary negative filter for gross behavioral errors. Mandate closed-loop Monte Carlo simulation sweeps across perturbed plant dynamics followed by isolated physical test-track execution before granting live tracking authority.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Web-style canary traffic routing is directly applicable to physical machines.*

In cloud software engineering, canary deployments route a small fraction of live user traffic to a newly deployed microservice, instantly rolling back if error rates spike. A robotics team adopts this pattern, assigning a similar fraction of active warehouse transport missions to an unvetted end-to-end foundation model. Unlike web requests, physical AI manipulates mass and momentum. A `{python} ReleaseBlindTravel.m1_str` vehicle moving at `{python} ReleaseBlindTravel.v_aisle_str` carries `{python} ReleaseBlindTravel.e_k_str` of kinetic energy; if an unvetted policy commands erratic acceleration toward a human coworker, the resulting collision cannot be undone by reverting a container image or rolling back a deployment replica set.

**Kinetic blast radius makes live production canary routing unviable without deterministic physical containment.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Permit canary deployments only within physically geofenced, human-excluded test zones, or behind an independent, non-preemptible permission path that preserves the assessed viable set under the declared sensing, plant, timing, and fault assumptions regardless of candidate proposals, with its stop carried by the rated lease watchdog and the certified drive functions.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Over-the-air updates can be treated as stateless software deployments.*

A replaceable stateless service can restart from an immutable image, although many cloud services also retain state. A robotics team adopts this paradigm, assuming that flashing an updated neural policy or real-time kernel over the air is identical to updating web services. However, physical AI systems possess persistent hardware state. Every machine carries individual physical calibration matrices (camera extrinsics, joint zero-position encoder offsets, and load-cell tare values) and mechanical wear histories. If an OTA update reformats the filesystem or fails to preserve the isolated calibration parameter partition, the newly deployed model operates with misaligned sensor frames. The stale transforms corrupt the localization allowance, creating perception offsets that the stopping argument did not charge.

**Physical AI deployments are inherently stateful; software cannot be divorced from individual machine calibration.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Decouple machine-specific physical calibrations into an isolated, schema-versioned EEPROM or protected flash partition that persists across OS bank swaps. Pair dual A/B partitioning with watchdog response that first places the plant in its assessed update state. Restore an image with its compatible calibration record only after current standing conditions pass.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Continuous high-bandwidth wireless telemetry streaming is superior to edge event-triggered buffering.*

To achieve complete operational visibility, an engineering team attempts to stream uncompressed multi-modal sensor data (dual camera streams, dense lidar point clouds, and 1 kHz motor current logs) continuously over facility Wi-Fi or cellular networks to cloud telemetry dashboards. Under dense fleet operations, wireless channel saturation, RF fading in industrial bays, and roaming handoffs cause massive packet loss and transmission queue bloat precisely during critical dynamic events. Furthermore, continuous network streaming consumes substantial onboard compute and bus bandwidth, risking memory bus contention that starves deterministic safety enforcers.

**Wireless bandwidth is physically finite and vulnerable to RF shadowing; streaming continuous raw sensor data drops the critical frames preceding a collision.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Stream compact health summaries and retain high-rate event traces locally. Qualify the pre-trigger and response window, storage bandwidth, and recording power under the declared faults, preserving required records until transfer succeeds without delaying protection.
:::

## Summary {#sec-release-summary}

Release decides which physical claims the evidence licenses for a named machine, under which conditions, and for how long. For the warehouse mobile manipulator the question becomes three inequalities: the base stops inside the surveyed clearance, the arm opens the door under the latch limit, and a handover stays under the contact criterion for a free hand. A claim-argument-evidence case\index{Safety case!claim-argument-evidence} links each inequality to its premises and evidence inside a named operating envelope\index{Operating envelope!release scope}. Required premises combine conjunctively, so the case is judged by its least supported premise, and only independent legs, such as the policy's evidence and the permission path, strengthen a claim beyond either alone. Machinery standards govern the argument, and within the permission path only the safety MCU's lease-expiry and heartbeat watchdog is a rated safety function.

The adjudicator resolves the case into `UNCOND`, `COND`, or `REFUSE`, and standing conditions withdraw the grant when a premise becomes false or unknown. One of those premises is administrative rather than physical: every record that identifies a person declares its purpose, retention period, and readers, and an access and retention audit suspends any use outside them (@sec-release-recorded-people). On this book's illustrative inputs every claim carries an ungrounded premise, so the verdict is `REFUSE`, while a stipulated branch shows which evidence would support restricted service. Adversarial review attacks the argument before signature and must recur in service. The signed manifest binds the verdict to the reviewed records by digest and fails closed on any mismatch, and every later update returns through the same argument, because shadow operation cannot test the physical consequences of a candidate's own actions.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Deployment release and safety cases"}

* **The envelope bounds the claim:** A release claim covers only the speeds, payloads, floors, clearances, and contact cases for which empirical evidence was gathered. Every dimension of the operational design domain requires an active runtime monitor or an enforced site operating regime.
* **Doubt accumulates along required premises:** A conjunctive argument ($\bigwedge_i C_i$) is no stronger than its weakest required premise and usually weaker, and it is never averaged. High empirical accuracy in perception cannot compensate for an unmonitored braking warrant or an uncharacterized tail latency. Only independent legs, such as the policy's evidence and the permission path, can do better, and only while their independence is itself evidenced.
* **Standing conditions make release revocable:** Each relied-on premise needs a detector or site procedure, a checking cadence, and a validated response when the premise becomes false or unknown. The signed case binds those obligations to the machine throughout operation.
* **The records that ground release also record people:** Takeover logs, aisle traces, and demonstration episodes identify operators and bystanders. Each such record declares its purpose, retention, and access as a standing condition, audited like any other, so the evidence a stop needs is kept and nothing becomes a surveillance record no release authorized.
* **Updates return through the release argument:** Shadow operation exposes candidate disagreements without testing their physical consequences. Closed-loop qualification and the reviewed manifest still govern release; a software update must preserve machine-specific calibration and a validated stop or hold during cutover.
* **An unknown premise refuses, and refusal names the next work:** Unknown envelope membership counts as outside the envelope, so on this book's illustrative inputs the mobile manipulator's verdict is `REFUSE`. The refusal identifies the missing measurement, the claim it would support, and the restriction that remains after a supporting result.
* **Useful service needs its own evidence:** The explicitly stipulated restricted mug-delivery branch reaches `COND` only by satisfying task-success, cycle-time, and rescue criteria alongside C1–C6. Normal filtering may preserve useful task success while raw proposer autonomy remains lower.
* **No verdict moves the proposal boundary:** Under `UNCOND` and `COND` alike, the policy only proposes and the permission path admits each action, with only its lease-expiry and heartbeat watchdog rated as a safety function. A restricted mode requires its own authenticated release case, never an ad-hoc runtime downgrade.
:::

The fourth law (@sec-boundary-bedrock-laws), stated as principle \ref{pri-vol4-evidence-bounds-authority}, grants authority on recorded evidence and lets it expire with that evidence, and the standing conditions are where that expiry becomes mechanism. Each pairs a premise with a detector, a cadence, and a response, so the loaded stopping trials that would support a conditional verdict for the mobile manipulator become, once signed, the evidence whose lapse ends it. On this book's actual records that grant never arrives, because each of the six claims rests on a premise left illustrative or unknown. The separately stipulated branch shows how supporting evidence would produce useful restricted service and which conditions would keep that grant valid. The manual lease limited an operator's authority to the age of its evidence (@sec-intervention-authority-transitions), and precommitment tied a test's verdict to a rule fixed before the evidence arrived (@sec-verification-oracles-acceptance). Release is the widest grant the book makes, and even there admission stays below the proposal boundary.

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-release-history}

The safety case began as a theory of argument before it became an engineering record. @toulmin1958uses separated practical reasoning into a claim, the data offered for it, the warrant that licenses the step, and the rebuttals that would defeat it, and that anatomy survives almost unchanged in the release argument of this chapter. Safety engineering gave it a notation in the late 1990s. The claim-argument-evidence methodology of @bishop1998methodology and the Goal Structuring Notation of @kelly1998arguing made the argument something a second engineer could check link by link, and ANSI/UL 4600 later carried the goal-based case to autonomous products, adding safety performance indicators and independent assessment [@ul4600].

Two results then fixed what such an argument may claim. @butler1993infeasibility showed that the failure rates demanded of life-critical software cannot be demonstrated by testing, and @kalra2016driving translated the same arithmetic into the distance an automated vehicle would have to drive, so a hazard claim needs an architectural warrant beside its trial record. @knight1986experimental showed that independently written versions of one program fail together more often than independence predicts, which is why a multi-legged argument [@bloomfield2003multilegged] must evidence the independence of its legs rather than assume it. That requirement became claim C5 of the running machine.

The last lesson concerns time. The Rogers Commission [@rogers1986challenger] and @vaughan1996challenger showed how an accepted argument erodes through a run of anomalies that each seemed harmless, with no single decision to blame. Dynamic safety cases [@denney2015dynamic] answered by keeping the argument live through operation, and compromise-resilient update frameworks [@samuel2010survivable; @kuppusamy2016uptane] made the channel that changes the machine part of what must be secured. This chapter joins those strands. It binds the verdict to a signed manifest that the machine checks before it moves, and it states every premise as a standing condition whose failure withdraws the grant.

For further reading, six works trace the ideas this chapter composes.

- @toulmin1958uses introduces the claim, warrant, and rebuttal structure on which every safety argument in this chapter is built, and shows why a warrant is a separate premise from the data.
- @bishop1998methodology sets out a claim-argument-evidence method for developing a safety case, the structure behind @tbl-16-cae-scorecard.
- @kelly1998arguing develops Goal Structuring Notation and the patterns for managing safety cases through change, the graph form of @fig-16-argument-graph.
- @knight1986experimental reports the multiversion experiment that rejected independent failure among diverse versions, the evidence behind treating independence as a claim to be tested.
- @vaughan1996challenger reconstructs the Challenger launch decision and names the normalization of deviance, the erosion that safety performance indicators exist to catch.
- @koopman2016challenges names inductive learning among the five challenges that an autonomous system poses to conventional validation, and proposes phased deployment under relaxed scenarios, a monitor and actuator pair that separates autonomy from the safety function, and fault injection, the same three moves this chapter's release makes.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From release to engineering judgment"}
What can the completed engineering argument support, and what must change to expand it? The actual textbook record remains refused; the stipulated branch supports a useful restricted mission with explicit friction, access, identity, and response premises. More trials with unchanged sensors cannot make transparent oil directly observable, but a qualified detector, a maintained exclusion regime, or a differently bounded task can change the argument. The conclusion, @sec-frontier, brings the book's engineering capabilities together and assigns each remaining premise an owner, restriction, and closure test.
:::

```{=latex}
\part{key:synthesis}
```
